items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: And Paul Whitman came himself to hear Fletcher's band, and he said, if Fletcher was a white man, he would be a millionaire.

ctx.x: No, I had not heard any. In fact, I hadn't heard about Louis at all. But after he arrived here, then you began to hear everything, yes, indeed. Louis was a great guy.

Well, Duke came to town. And he was playing at the Kentucky Club, 48th Street and Broadway. Now, you know, in those days, it wasn't so many musicians, and Fletcher's band was the top band. And Paul Whitman had been named just a couple of years ago the King of Jazz. He was a violinist. And Paul Whitman came himself to hear Fletcher's band, and he said, if Fletcher was a white man, he would be a millionaire. That's just what he said. I heard him.
Well, Fletcher went up and up and up and up and up.
